attempts.label: DANDI:001544
attempts.paper_title: Distinct subpopulations of ventral pallidal cholinergic projection neurons encode valence of olfactory stimuli
attempts.entry_title: Intrinsic excitability of odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons (Kim et al. 2024)
attempts.summary: Only the patch-clamp findings could be tested, and higher maximum firing in odor-activated than home-cage neurons held. Greater hyperpolarization of aversive-odor neurons, their smaller afterhyperpolarization and lower excitability of appetitive-odor neurons did not. For hyperpolarization, resting potential cannot be measured, as every recording is under a holding current. The behavior, cFos, photometry, chemogenetic, reactivation and morphology findings could not be tested, because those data are not in the dandiset. Minor results on sag and other features depend on which 21 of 24 home-cage cells the paper used.
attempts.description: Tests the electrophysiological findings of Kim, Ananth, Desai, Role and Talmage (2024) on dandiset 001544, which holds current-clamp recordings of 44 ventral pallidal cholinergic neurons labelled as activated by an appetitive odor, by an aversive odor, or from home-cage mice. It compares the maximum firing rate, sag, membrane potential, afterhyperpolarization, excitability and the other features of the paper's Methods between the three groups. The behaviour, histology, fiber photometry and morphology of the paper are not in the dandiset.

Max firing rate ALL 12.5, APP 50.5, AV 49.25 Hz over 24, 12 and 8 cells. Reading (a) F(2, 41) = 10.83 (paper 10.71); ALL against APP t(34) = 5.07, p = 1.4e-05 (paper t(31) = 5.36); ALL against AV t(30) = 3.91, p = 0.00049 (paper t(27) = 2.80). Reading (b), mixed model, p = 0.00085 and 0.0098. Both pairs stay below 0.05 without the `_FL` cells (21 ALL, F(2, 38) = 9.80), without the cells whose test-pulse resistance changed by more than 20% (p 0.0011 to 0.024) and with all steps in the file as the code takes them (p 6.6e-05 to 0.025). Per mouse, APP means 4 to 87 Hz, AV 13 to 90, ALL 4 to 29. With the mixed-model contrasts referred to t on 18 df (mice minus 3), p = 0.0037 and 0.019. The Methods' switch to non-parametric tests would apply (Shapiro-Wilk p 0.00023), and they agree, Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.0030, Mann-Whitney ALL against APP p = 0.0023 and ALL against AV p = 0.022.
deviations: The dandiset holds 24 ALL cells from 11 mice where the paper analysed 21 from 8, and does not say which were left out. All 24 are used (assumed, as the dataset labels them), with the 21 cells left when the three `_FL` files are set aside, and the cells passing the 20% change rule, shown as variants.

Reading (b), the nested ANOVA of the STAR Methods (Quantification and statistical analysis, "a nested ANOVA was run to account for replicate values obtained from the same mouse"), is fitted as a linear mixed model with a random intercept per mouse (REML) and Wald tests against the normal, with the same contrasts against t on the number of mice minus 3 df and the classical nested F beside them; the paper does not give its software's model beyond Prism or SigmaPlot.

Exclusion rules (STAR Methods, Electrophysiology). Input resistance under 50 MOhm and resting potential above -50 mV exclude no cell. Series resistance is not in the files. The 20% change rule was read through the -20 pA test pulse of each sweep, first sweep against last; it would remove 2 APP, 2 AV and 10 ALL cells, which does not fit the dandiset's APP and AV counts already equalling the paper's, so it is a variant, not the main set.
Spike detection, the step window and the f-I slope follow the paper's code, nsdesai/patch_clamp_analysis v1.0.0 (commit 4ee1125), as the claims file says.

Only steps from -60 to 200 pA are used (STAR Methods, Electrophysiology, "-60 to 200 pA amplitude", and item 16, "a current step between 0 and 200 pA"); the code's use of every step in the file is a variant.

The STAR Methods (Quantification and statistical analysis) say "Non-parametric tests were conducted if the data failed these tests" (Shapiro-Wilk and Kolmogorov-Smirnov). The claims file's readings do not include this rule, so the outcome follows readings (a) and (b), and Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney results are shown beside them; a question for a reader is in questions/001544.yaml.

outcomes.notes: Sag ALL 3.22, APP 6.68, AV 4.90 mV on all 44 cells. AV does not exceed ALL under either reading (t = 1.77, p = 0.087; mixed model p = 0.24, 0.25 with t on 18 df), so the criterion, which needs both groups, fails. APP exceeds ALL by both parametric readings (t = 2.71, p = 0.011; mixed model p = 0.0041, 0.010 with t on 18 df) but not by the non-parametric tests the Methods prescribe when normality fails (Shapiro-Wilk p = 0.0016; Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.12; Mann-Whitney ALL against APP p = 0.10, ALL against AV p = 0.094). Five cells (four APP, one ALL) sit at -105.62 mV for 45 to 463 ms of the -60 pA step, which clips their minimum and underestimates their sag (one other APP file, 20221214_001, passes that value and reaches -112.88 mV, so it is not a floor in every file). With the next unsaturated step for them neither pair holds (p = 0.053 and 0.085); leaving them out, APP exceeds ALL (p = 0.016; mixed model p = 0.017) and AV does not (p = 0.092; mixed model p = 0.13). Without the `_FL` cells reading (a) gives both pairs (p = 0.0036 and 0.0072) and reading (b) misses AV (p = 0.12), so on that set the readings would disagree; without the cells whose test-pulse resistance changed by more than 20% neither pair holds (p = 0.18 and 0.086). Changed in revision from partially_reproduced (see verifications). outcomes.notes: Judged on the ten features the Figure S12 legend names as similar, as the claims file now has it. By the cell-level one-way ANOVA, 9 of the 10 show no difference on all cells (threshold, upstroke, spike amplitude, spike latency, AHP width, CV of ISIs, rheobase, tau, adaptation index); AHP latency differs (p = 0.012, APP 24.9 ms against ALL 48.6 and AV 56.8). The count is 7 of 10 without the `_FL` cells (rheobase p = 0.045 and adaptation index p = 0.040 also differ) and 10 of 10 without the cells whose resistance changed by more than 20%; the mixed model gives 9, 7 and 10. Adaptation index, marked with an asterisk in the figure, has p = 0.056 on all cells. By Kruskal-Wallis, the Methods' test when normality fails, the count is 7 of 10 on all cells (spike latency, AHP latency and adaptation index differ), 6 of 10 without the `_FL` cells and 9 of 10 without the changed cells, still more than half. What the answer changed. The question asked whether the claim should be judged on the legend's ten features in place of the fourteen (the eighteen of the Methods less max firing rate, sag, membrane potential and AHP amplitude). On the ten, every cell set and both tests give more than half, so the outcome no longer rests on which ALL cells are used and is no longer marked assumed.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only the current-clamp step recordings of Figure 6 and Figure S12. The behaviour, immunohistochemistry counts, fiber photometry, chirp recordings and neuronal reconstructions are not in it, and the paper's data statement says all data will be shared by the lead contact on request. 24 of the 31 claims in the claims file cannot be tested.
Every CurrentClampStimulusSeries is stated in amperes with conversion 1, but holds values from -60 to 500, the step amplitudes in picoamperes.

The DC current that holds each cell near -65 mV is not recorded; `bias_current` (1e-11 A) and `bridge_balance` (2e7 Ohm) hold the same value in all 44 files, which a holding current set per cell cannot. No segment of any sweep is free of the holding current, so the resting potential the Methods define ("measured in the absence of a current injection") cannot be obtained.

The home-cage (ALL) group holds 24 cells from 11 mice, where the Figure 6 legend reports 21 cells from 8 mice; the dandiset does not say which cells the paper left out or why. No 8 of the 11 mice hold 21 cells (any 8 hold 14 to 20), so the paper's set is not the deposit less whole mice. The APP (12 cells, 6 mice) and AV (8 cells, 4 mice) groups match the legend.
The six APP mice are 4 male and 2 female in the files, where the Figure 6 legend says 3 male and 3 female.
Five ALL mice (CG354, CG355, CG382, CG538, CG539; 9 cells) are 5.7 to 6.6 weeks old in the files, younger than the 8 to 12 weeks the STAR Methods give for all mice.

Every sweep's starting_time is 0, so the order in time and the 10 s between steps are not recorded; series resistance is not recorded, so that exclusion rule cannot be checked. Three files carry suffixes `_NSD` and `_FL` on their identifiers, with no description; the two CG538 files sharing recording number 003 are different cells (input resistance 192 and 802 MOhm), and the `_FL` files use 5 s sweeps where all others use 2 s.

Five recordings (four APP, one ALL) reach -105.6 mV and stay there for 10 ms or more during the -60 pA step, flat at that value, which truncates the response; sag measured on these sweeps is underestimated. The value is not a floor in every file: one other APP file (20221214_001) has 7 samples at -105.62 mV and 1735 below -105.7 mV, down to -112.88 mV. Three sweeps hold NaN for their last 0.1 to 0.6 s, after the step.

The paper's code (v1.0.0) differs from the Methods in the spike threshold (10 against 20 mV/ms), spike latency (to the peak, not the threshold), AHP amplitude (minimum to the next spike on the first step with two spikes, not within 100 ms at rheobase) and tau (the -40 pA step, not -20 pA). Its downstroke window runs to the end of the step, and its test for a saturated sag response never fires (it compares with 1000 the count of the most frequent index among the unchanged samples, which is always 1).

The STAR Methods say a nested ANOVA was run for the electrophysiology to account for cells from the same mouse, but the reported degrees of freedom (F(2, 38), t(31), t(27), t(18)) are those of cell-level tests on 41 cells.

The Results say the convex hull of APP neurons was smaller than that of AV neurons in surface area and volume (Figure S13C), but the Figure S13 legend lists the volume of the convex hull among the features with no significant difference between the groups.

Question for the paper's authors. Which 21 of the 24 home-cage cells (and which 8 of the 11 mice) were analysed, and how was the rule on a 20% change of series resistance, input resistance or resting potential applied? The outcomes of figs12a-sag-higher and figs12-app-differs-from-all here change with the cell set (sag of AV against ALL p = 0.087 on all 24 cells, 0.0072 without the three `_FL` cells; in the set passing the 20% change rule, 3 of the 4 APP-specific features differ by reading (a) and 2 by reading (b)). And how was the membrane potential of Figure 6G measured "in the absence of a current injection", when the files hold only sweeps under the DC holding current?

entries.name: 001544-kim-2024
entries.title: Intrinsic excitability of odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons (Kim et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the electrophysiological findings of Kim, Ananth, Desai, Role and Talmage (2024) on dandiset 001544, which holds current-clamp recordings of 44 ventral pallidal cholinergic neurons labelled as activated by an appetitive odor, by an aversive odor, or from home-cage mice. It compares the maximum firing rate, sag, membrane potential, afterhyperpolarization, excitability and the other features of the paper's Methods between the three groups. The behaviour, histology, fiber photometry and morphology of the paper are not in the dandiset.
